PetroVietnam Oil Nam Dinh JSC Reports Solid Quarterly Earnings Amid Stable Domestic Demand

HANOI, Vietnam, June 19 — PetroVietnam Oil Nam Dinh JSC, a key player in Vietnam’s oil and gas production sector, reported steady quarterly earnings on Wednesday, attributing the performance to resilient domestic fuel demand and effective cost management.

For the quarter ended March 31, the company posted a net profit of 87 billion dong ($3.4 million), a 5% increase from the same period last year. Revenue rose 4.2% year-on-year to 1.53 trillion dong, driven by sustained sales of refined petroleum products and stable wholesale contracts across the northern provinces.

“Our financial results reflect the underlying strength of Vietnam’s energy market and our commitment to operational efficiency,” said Le Quoc Minh, chief executive officer of PetroVietnam Oil Nam Dinh JSC, in a statement. “Despite global price volatility, domestic consumption has remained robust, supporting our continued growth.”

The company said sales volumes remained above 200,000 cubic meters for the quarter, with gasoline and diesel accounting for the majority of its product mix. The average realized selling price increased slightly, in line with broader regional trends.

Industry analysts say the results are in line with expectations, noting that Vietnam’s economic recovery and ongoing infrastructure projects have supported fuel demand. “The downstream sector has held up well, thanks to steady industrial activity and government investments in transportation,” said Nguyen Van Hoang, energy analyst at Asia Pacific Research Partners.

Operating expenses edged lower year-on-year, as the company continued to optimize logistics and procurement processes. Le Quoc Minh highlighted recent investments in digital inventory management and upgraded storage facilities at Nam Dinh port, which he said have improved supply chain resilience and reduced costs.

The company’s board announced an interim dividend of 500 dong per share, unchanged from the previous quarter, reflecting confidence in cash flow stability. Shareholders are set to meet in August to review the firm’s long-term capital expenditure plans.

Vietnam’s oil and gas producers have benefited from relatively stable domestic demand even as international crude prices fluctuate. The Vietnam Petroleum Association reported that nationwide fuel consumption grew 3.7% in the first quarter, with imports supplementing local refinery output.

Looking ahead, PetroVietnam Oil Nam Dinh JSC said it remains focused on expanding its retail network and enhancing sustainability initiatives, including pilot programs for biofuel blending.
